messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT 23:05 UTC — spike in KV cache evictions + continuous-batching amplification detected for region-us-west. Metric: evictions/sec x10, avg latency p95 -> 420ms. Triggering pager to on-call.
Alice (oncall): on it, joining channel. seeing throttles on kv-reader nodes? grabbing dashboards now. :eyes:
Kelsey (eng-sre): I see a correlated rise in microbatch queue lengths starting ~22:58 UTC. Looks like batch window shrank and led to more small batches -> cache churn.
Ravi (eng-runtime): confirmed. recent rolling deploy of microbatch-scheduler (rev f3a9c) included a default batch_target_ms change from 30 -> 10. Might explain amplification on short seq workloads.
Mei (eng-infra): any single-tenant hot customer hit? I can spin per-customer overrides if needed.
Sam_CS: Customer "BrightMart" reporting increased 5xxs on embedding endpoints. They are in us-west. Escalating with them.
Alice (oncall): plan: 1) quick mitigate by flipping batch_target_ms back for affected hosts via feature flag 2) enable per-customer cap for BrightMart to limit concurrency 3) monitor evictions. Ravi/Mei, can you prepare flag and override?
Ravi (eng-runtime): creating hotfix flag now. Flag key: runtime.microbatch.batch_target_ms.override. Intend to set to 30ms for affected pool.
Ravi (eng-runtime): patch command: ```
curl -X POST "https://flags.internal/api/v1/flags/toggle" -d '{"flag":"runtime.microbatch.batch_target_ms.override","value":30,"scope":"pool:us-west-microbatch"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
```
Kelsey (eng-sre): rolling the flag to 10% canary first on non-prod-like subset? But BrightMart is high-risk; suggest immediate 100% for pools serving them and 10% elsewhere.
Mei (eng-infra): I can push per-customer throttle: ```
rbctl set-customer-limit --customer-id=brightmart --max-concurrency=4 --kv-cache-evict-protect=true
```
Alice (oncall): do it. Ravi, flip the flag for pools with brightmart traffic only. Post the flag response.
Ravi (eng-runtime): flag applied for pool:us-west-microbatch hosts 12/12 serving brightmart. API response: {"status":"ok","applied":true}. Rolling to additional 10% test group now.
Kelsey (eng-sre): monitoring: evictions/sec on target pool dropped from 1200 -> 160 within 90s. p95 latency trending down. BrightMart 5xxs falling. :thumbsup:
Sam_CS: Confirmed BrightMart sees errors clear. They reported back to CS. Thank you.
Jordan (product): any customer-visible data loss? We need to notify support if we have to throttle.
Alice (oncall): no data loss, only higher latencies and some 503s. Mei's per-customer cap prevents overload; will keep cap.\nKelsey (eng-sre): FYI metrics: cache hitrate improved from 61% -> 87% after flag. KV paging events subsided.
Ravi (eng-runtime): follow-up: creating a rolling hotfix PR to revert default batch_target_ms to 30ms and add a safe-guard telemetry gate. Will link in thread.
Ravi (eng-runtime): PR: https://git.internal/runtime/merge_requests/512 — includes canary config for flagging by customer-id and auto-fallback.
Mei (eng-infra): scheduled per-customer cap removal window: will keep for 2 hours post-stable, then drop to monitoring-only.
Alice (oncall): ops checklist: 
- keep flag live on affected pools 
- keep BrightMart cap for 2 hours 
- watch evictions, p95 latency, 5xx rate 
- if any regression, rollback flag and re-enable previous routing fallback
Kelsey (eng-sre): will run query to enumerate other customers with similar seq distributions and batch pressure. Might preemptively open per-cust overrides for top 3 at-risk tenants.
Sam_CS: looping in support to email BrightMart post-incident note and let them know we applied a temporary throttle and permanent fix PR in flight.
Alice (oncall): timeline so far: 22:58 UTC — deploy rev f3a9c changed default batch_target_ms. 23:05 UTC — incident detected and paged. 23:08 UTC — flag applied to BrightMart-serving pool. 23:10 UTC — per-customer cap enabled. 23:12 UTC — errors falling. 23:19 UTC — metrics stable.
Kelsey (eng-sre): next steps: run post-incident eval, add regression alert for batch_target_ms changes, and add a canary gate to prevent immediate global rollout of microbatch-scheduler defaults.
Ravi (eng-runtime): added templated alert: "continuous_batching_amplification" with runbook link.
Alice (oncall): handing off to Kelsey for postmortem and long-term mitigation. I'm clear after confirming stables for 1h.
Kelsey (eng-sre): taking over. I'll create incident ticket and assign owners for PR + follow-up testing. Tagging: @ravi, @mei, @sam_cs.
IncidentBot: Incident acknowledged by Kelsey (eng-sre) at 23:25 UTC. Incident severity: Sev2 -> mitigated.
Kelsey (eng-sre): quick note to add to ticket: customer-impact window 22:58-23:19 UTC, affected customer(s): BrightMart, approx 7k requests impacted, root cause: unguarded default change to microbatch scheduler reducing batch_target_ms causing more small batches and KV cache churn. Remediation: hotflag revert + per-customer cap + PR for safe canary.
Alice (oncall): leaving channel. ping if anything else. :wave:
Kelsey (eng-sre): thanks all. I'll draft the summary and link dashboards + logs.
Jordan (product): include note about opt-in canary for customers with high short-seq workloads; product will coordinate communication.
Ravi (eng-runtime): log snippet for context: ```
[22:59:03] WARN microbatch: small_batch_rate=0.88 batch_target_ms=10 pool=us-west-microbatch evictions=842
[23:06:12] INFO microbatch: applied-flag runtime.microbatch.batch_target_ms.override=30 scope=pool:us-west-microbatch
```
Kelsey (eng-sre): closing note: mitigation successful, next: postmortem + runbook updates. Will create artifacts in #incidents and link here.
